original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Is there an exact helper-donor kernel (one deleted read plus compensating reads) on the pending T74 pivot-566+554 base word when the compensating reads may use several linearly dependent values (split keys), not only multiples of the deleted read's source value? Domain: every A-section deletion (first full relaxation) and every kernel-sized deletion (gain -3,050 to -8,857) in A and B.
scope_change_reason: The card targets the selected k8 packing. In the open kappa claims (PR1928 and predecessors), PR1673's capped outer puts kappa within 1e-10010 of the T74 complex supplier's own saving, so a cheaper T74 local word is the only route to a kappa gain there. The last two gains on that supplier (PR1625, PR1672) were single helper-donor kernels of -1,850 units, and PR1957 exhausted only the same-key compensation family on 16+85+5 sampled reads. This package widens the move family and completes the A-section relaxation.
bottleneck_link: Each previous helper-donor kernel (-1,850 cost units on both words: H1 +666, H2 -1,332, H3 +666 globally) raised the T74 endpoint, hence the pending kappa, by about 4.1e-8. A third kernel would be a real (small) kappa gain; this package shows none exists in the searched family on the base word.
stop_rule: Stop when every kernel-sized deletion (deletion gain -3,050 to -8,857, the range where one rank-2 compensating split could still leave a profit) on the base word has a split-key search that CP-SAT proves infeasible or that is shape-infeasible, or as soon as one exact profitable kernel is found. Larger structural deletions (data butterflies, delivery reads) are out of scope.
evidence: RESULTS.json (recomputed by tools/summarize.py). Full A-section deletion relaxation: 3,451 gates (3,124 first priced here). Split-key searches: every kernel-sized deletion in A and B; all proven infeasible or shape-infeasible, zero exact profitable kernels. Positive control: the same search rediscovers PR1672's k554-signed-001 kernel (-1,850, exact) on the pivot-566-only word. Diagnostics: with the per-insert cost filter loosened to 3x budget and no summed budget, the deleted read itself is the unique exact compensation for B783 and B802.

open_questions.question: Does an exact profitable kernel exist when compensating inserts may interact (an insert writes a register that a later insert reads)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without the interaction ban, the first-order model proposed zero-oracle-cost compensations for B783 that were inexact only because of such interactions; the interacting family is not excluded here.
open_questions.first_step: Take an interacting first-order proposal, compute its exact residual map (base map minus edited map), and run a second split-key round whose right-hand side is that residual.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a residual-repair (or exact bilinear) search model; not implemented in this session.

open_questions.question: Do the same searches fail on the extra word (417 of the 666 T74 calls)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All searches here use the base gauge44 word only. Previous kernels applied identically to both words, but a kernel valid on the extra word alone would still raise the endpoint.
open_questions.first_step: Run tools/skkernel.py on research/t74-k554-local-exhaustion/inputs/extra-word-566.json.gz for B783/B802 and the A1215-A1246 pre-cancels, after re-running PR1957's relaxations on that word to confirm the same gain map.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute: roughly 20 minutes of relaxation on 11 cores plus about 2 minutes per -6,763 search.

open_questions.question: Can a larger key family (recursing through registers added into the source or target) admit a kernel for the four B reads at -6,100 that remain shape-infeasible?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Shape infeasibility means some affected output row has no candidate in the present one-level family; a wider family is the cheapest way to reach it.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the key family to the values held by and added into every register that is added into the source or target, then rerun B822/B840/B858/B876.
open_questions.blocked_by: Candidate generation is pure Python; the -8,857 accumulator jobs already take about 5 minutes with 52 keys.
